clue.text: Sad and is close to tears

indicators.note: tears as a verb means rips apart, so the letters before it are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of someone so unhappy they are near to crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping; it is the verb meaning rips, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconsolable is deeply unhappy and beyond comfort.

indicators.note: as an adjective fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters before it are dressed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admires a rifle, thinking the slope of it rather fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as a speaker's opinion; 'I' is part of the fodder and 'fancy' the anagram signal. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack or plunder it, which is to strip it of goods.

clue.text: Turf out of small hospital room

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a ward is a room in a hospital holding several beds

explanation.surface: An order to throw someone out of a small hospital room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turf out' looks like one phrasal verb; 'Turf' alone is the definition and 'out of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is an expanse of short grass, the same stuff as a stretch of lawn.

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body, so the speech holds the other letters within it

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters, with the inside gone

explanation.surface: A politician's campaign address that is padded with hollow prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' means hollowed out, keeping just the shell of the word, so only its outer letters go into the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A military campaign or planned series of actions is also called an operation.

indicators.note: pressed into something, so the wife's letter is pushed inside the word for sink

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies and records

explanation.surface: Loot that a wife was struck by when it sank in.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods, the spoils of a robbery.

clue.text: Subject of fiction with grand title elevated

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untrue story
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means lifted upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a title is the name of a book or work

explanation.surface: A topic in fiction, with a grand title raised high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' poses as a topic of study; here it is a person subject to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal bound to serve a lord was that lord's subject.

clue.text: Sovereign state of Georgia supporting great weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: a ton is a large unit of weight
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A sovereign state of Georgia, the former Soviet republic, propping up a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign state of Georgia' reads as one phrase; 'of' is a link and Georgia is the US state, GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an independent Pacific island kingdom, a country in its own right.

indicators.note: redesigning something rearranges its parts, so these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework menus using oil paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil paint' looks like one item; 'oil' is fodder and only 'paint' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a common water-based wall paint used in home decorating.

indicators.note: the bikini bottom is worn by the runs, so it goes round them

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy lower half of a bikini
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A beach host jogging in nothing but a skimpy bikini bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great crowd, as in a multitude of people.

parts.note: stale means no longer fresh, old
a mate is a friend or pal

explanation.surface: An old friend handing over a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like a necktie but is a drawn result.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn position in chess or a deadlock in a dispute is a tie with no winner.

clue.text: Originally nubile young maiden, pretty hot!

definitions.text: Originally nubile young maiden, pretty hot!

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so each word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation about an attractive young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the starting letters spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology and poetry a nymph is a beautiful young maiden spirit.

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the over and agreement pieces hold the Republican letter

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A court trial about a deal that involved a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' reads as a court case; here it is a painful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or testing experience is both a trial and a tribulation.

clue.text: Place for women galore is fantastic!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly imaginative, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a place with women in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the harem quarters of a Muslim palace, set aside for wives and concubines.

clue.text: Young male tot having rest outside

indicators.note: outside means the rest goes round the tot

parts.note: to lie is to rest
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A little boy, a tot, having a rest outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' poses as a small child but is the verb meaning add; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is a Scottish familiar word for a boy or lad.

clue.text: Soldiers and sergeant finally in action, barking

indicators.note: in places the soldiers and the letter inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
men is a common word for soldiers, ordinary ranks

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers and their sergeant in battle, shouting orders like mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' suggests a shouting sergeant, but it is British slang for mad, as in barking mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking is British slang for crazy, and demented means out of one's mind.

clue.text: Fixing old man caught in whatsit

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: in puts the caught letter inside the word for whatsit

parts.note: a whatsit is a thing whose name escapes you
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A father repairing some gadget and getting caught up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Patching up a hole or tear is mending it, a way of repairing.

indicators.note: conceals means hiding within, so the bond holds the other letters

parts.note: a charter is a written deed or bond granting rights
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: James Bond hiding a chilly charm beneath his manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy; it is a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm or magic sign is an old sense of a written symbol, as with letters in a spell.

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sensitive body part that is rather ticklish.
explanation.definitionFit: An artistic temperament is one alert to beauty and feeling, finely tuned and responsive.

indicators.note: follows sets the word for never after the word for house

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home
nary is a dialect word meaning not one, never

explanation.surface: A religious house that never follows the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college that trains priests or ministers, a religious institution.

indicators.note: a deserted word has lost its inhabitants, the inner letters, leaving only the outside

parts.note: a line is a channel of communication, as a phone line

explanation.surface: Salt taken from an abandoned sea channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted sea' gives SA; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A saline solution is salt dissolved in water, so saline is salty or a salt solution.

clue.text: Hammered and tried to find gold

definitions.meaning: hammered here means harshly criticised, as in a review
prospectors swirl river gravel in a dish to search for gold

explanation.surface: A drunk gold prospector sifting a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' looks like drunk or beaten; it is slang for severely criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who slates a play pans it, and a prospector washing gravel also pans.

clue.text: Break up gang led by detectives

indicators.note: led by puts the detectives ahead of the gang

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors in the British police
a band is a group or gang

explanation.surface: Detectives leading a raid to break up a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband a group is to dissolve it, ending its existence as a unit.

clue.text: Underwear that is put on last

indicators.note: put on means the first piece is placed onto the end of the second

parts.note: to last is to linger or endure
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Underwear is the final garment you put on, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like final but is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Result of European Union's almost fresh upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom up

parts.note: U for Union plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: almost means nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: new means fresh

explanation.surface: The European Union's latest troubles result from a new crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost fresh' gives NE; with E, U and S, the lot is reversed by 'upset'. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, to come about as a result.

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for auctions

parts.note: auctions are sales

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the head, so the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Furs mainly bought at auction houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sables are the luxurious dark furs of a small Asian marten.

parts.note: a crown prince is the obvious picture, but the monarch is a butterfly, which starts as a caterpillar

explanation.surface: A young heir to the throne who has not yet grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch here is the orange and black butterfly, not a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the immature feeding stage of a butterfly, before it pupates.

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A stray animal that comes with a health condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, neglected child or animal, one that has strayed.

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so a word that sounds alike is entered

parts.note: kneads means works muscles with the hands, massages

explanation.surface: Young women supplying massages, it is rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' poses as young women; it is the verb meaning lacks. 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something you lack is to want it, to require it.

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the assembled pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly
OTT, over the top, means showy and flamboyant
art is skill, as in the art of cooking

explanation.surface: A display of showy skill supporting a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support; here it reverses AIR, OTT and ART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eatery serving simple food.

clue.text: From France, how red alters from now on?

indicators.note: alters means changes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about how French red wine will change in future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' at the start is a link; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforward is a formal adverb meaning starting at this point in time.
